Liverpool’s left-back Andy Robertson has highlighted the importance of tightening up the team's defence as a central factor in pursuing Premier League glory under new manager Arne Slot. While Slot has settled quickly into his new role, Liverpool’s backline has been equally impressive at the start of the season, not allowing a single goal in their first two fixtures. However, with an upcoming clash away at Manchester United, Liverpool’s defensive resilience faces a significant test—something their previous opponents, Ipswich Town and Brentford, failed to provide. Reflecting on last season, Robertson noted that Liverpool’s defensive record had left considerable room for improvement. The 41 goals they let in over the 38-match campaign saw them finish third in the league, with title-winners Manchester City conceding only 34 and Arsenal 29. Despite that shortcoming, there is genuine optimism around the early displays this term, which have shown a more robust unit at the back.

Handle tough opposition is always a key part of football seasons, particularly for clubs with title ambitions. Robertson emphasised the value of the two consecutive clean sheets, something Liverpool’s squad are eager to replicate as the fixtures grow more challenging. According to Robertson, restricting opponents’ chances as much as possible must remain a top priority—not only in the looming showdown against Manchester United, but also throughout the demanding calendar that picks up again after the international break. Drawing upon last season’s experiences, he admitted that even when Liverpool were firmly in the title race, their defensive vulnerability was a consistent issue. Both Arsenal and Manchester City were better at suppressing their rivals’ scoring opportunities. Robertson alluded to the idea that, when a club’s defence allows too many chances, there is always the risk of a match arriving where costly mistakes are inevitably punished—an outcome that unfortunately befell Liverpool last year.

Beyond the immediate uptick in defensive solidity, the message from the Liverpool camp is clear: sustained defensive excellence must underpin the team’s ambitions under the Slot regime. Keeping clean sheets builds confidence not only among defenders but throughout the squad, and sets the foundation for a genuine title challenge. The willingness to learn from past problems and immediately rectify them is a hallmark of successful teams, and according to Robertson’s comments, this is the mentality currently driving Liverpool forward. As Slot begins to stamp his authority and style on the club, the promising defensive start is seen as a possible sign of better things to come. With tougher assignments on the horizon, Liverpool’s ability to keep out goals could prove decisive in their quest to compete at the very top once again.

P.S. It’s always inspiring to see how a new manager and fresh focus can energise a club and its players, especially after a tough previous season. Let’s watch closely to see whether these early defensive improvements truly translate into a sustained run for the title!
